# Value-ref false-positive handling

Lifecycle status: accepted

During value-reference validation, false-positive clusters must be fixed while isolated singletons are recorded as known residuals. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 instructs agents to hunt FPs during the validation sweep, fix FP clusters, and record singletons.

# Sibling class constant ambiguity

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file-wide class-scope target map accepts a residual false-positive risk when sibling classes in the same file define the same constant name. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A says this is the only real false-positive case, observed at about 1.7% of Ruby targets on Rails, and valid code rarely hits it because a bare sibling-class constant is a Ruby NameError.

# Pascal case-sensitive misses

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value-reference scanning may miss references that differ only by case because Pascal is case-insensitive while the reader scan matches exact text; this is a false negative, not a false positive. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says differently-cased Pascal references are missed and not worth normalizing.

# Pascal const-param parse residual

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value refs accept a small residual false-positive tail where tree-sitter-pascal can context-dependently misparse a complex Delphi `const` parameter as `declConst`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 says this parse-fidelity FP remains after restricting Pascal targets to `constant` only and is documented as an accepted caveat.

item.text: I’ve got a candidate set of constraint notes. I’m now checking each one for a separate rationale record so I only return the constraints that truly lack a recorded rationale.

content.text:
Top 5 recorded entries:

# Watch sync stale-edge tolerance

Lifecycle status: accepted

Watch sync drops a single stale edge instead of aborting the whole daemon sync with a `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` error. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

# Watch sync pipeline

Lifecycle status: accepted

The watch sync pipeline is CodeGraph's file-watcher and incremental synchronization layer that keeps the index aligned with filesystem edits, git pulls, branch switches, and MCP reconnects. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 releases 0.9.5 and 0.9.6 describe watcher excludes, filesystem-based change detection, catch-up on connect, debounce tuning, and stale-lock handling.

# Manual sync after watcher distrust

Lifecycle status: accepted

When live watching cannot be trusted, users must rely on `codegraph sync` or git sync hooks until auto-sync is restored. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says CodeGraph disables auto-sync once with a clear message instead of retrying forever or serving a stale index as healthy.

# Stale files must be named

Lifecycle status: accepted

When watcher-observed edits are not yet indexed, CodeGraph responses must tell the agent exactly which files are stale instead of silently serving a stale graph as fresh. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 releases 0.9.5 and 0.9.6 say tool responses add a warning banner naming stale files and watcher sync keeps files stale while another process holds the index lock.

# Inotify limit partial watch

Lifecycle status: accepted

On Linux inotify exhaustion, CodeGraph reports the exact watch-limit setting and keeps watching the directories it could register. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says it names `fs.inotify.max_user_watches`, gives an example sysctl command, and relies on sync/git hooks for the rest.

content.text:
Top 5 recorded entries:

# Adoption metrics over token cost

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph adoption work must optimize wall-clock time, tool-call count, and Read=0 rather than treating token cost as the primary target. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 states this doctrine constraint explicitly and notes token cost is lower as a side effect.

# Replace implementation Reads

Lifecycle status: accepted

Agents should use CodeGraph instead of `Read`/`grep` during implementation, with success measured by wall-clock time, tool-call count, and Read=0 rather than token cost. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 frames P1 as agents still reaching for `Read`/`grep` and states the optimization target is wall-clock + tool-call count + Read=0, not token cost.

# Read hook worsened metrics

Lifecycle status: accepted

The blanket Read-deny hook achieved file-view usage but worsened the target metrics on a simple edit. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 reports hook runs at 8-9 tool calls, 9-10 turns, and 200-239s versus no-hook runs at 5-7 tool calls, 6-8 turns, and 55-77s.

# Reject blanket Read-deny hook

Lifecycle status: accepted

The blanket Read-deny redirect hook must not ship as the CodeGraph adoption mechanism. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says the hook was A/B'd and REJECTED, kept only as an eval artifact, because it regressed target metrics and the agent routed around it.

# Watcher cost stays flat

Lifecycle status: accepted

The recursive and bounded watcher design keeps CodeGraph's background watch cost flat with project size and avoids machine-wide file-descriptor exhaustion. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says unrelated apps previously failed after the watcher piled up tens of thousands of handles, and the new strategy keeps cost flat regardless of project size.

# Low-value ranking for sizing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Demoting or ranking low-value files is an ineffective way to shrink adaptive explore output because the budget is refilled with other full bodies. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 1 says broadening `isLowValuePath` barely changed size, from 28,478 to 28,424, and concludes ranking is not shrinking.

# Trezor facade skip

Lifecycle status: deprecated

CodeGraph skips the trezor connect-common/factory facade because it is low-value: it has a single call fan-in and does not disambiguate per-method targets. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 Immediate next actions says the facade remains low-value and should be skipped.

# Sizing requires skeletonization

Lifecycle status: accepted

Explore output size only shrinks when bodies are skeletonized, not when low-value files are merely demoted or ranked lower. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 1 says demoting low-value files improved content quality but not size because explore refilled the freed budget, and concludes that ranking is not shrinking.

Lifecycle status: accepted

During value-reference validation, false-positive clusters must be fixed while isolated singletons are recorded as known residuals. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 instructs agents to hunt FPs during the validation sweep, fix FP clusters, and record singletons.

# Pascal case-sensitive misses

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value-reference scanning may miss references that differ only by case because Pascal is case-insensitive while the reader scan matches exact text; this is a false negative, not a false positive. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says differently-cased Pascal references are missed and not worth normalizing.

# Sibling class constant ambiguity

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file-wide class-scope target map accepts a residual false-positive risk when sibling classes in the same file define the same constant name. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A says this is the only real false-positive case, observed at about 1.7% of Ruby targets on Rails, and valid code rarely hits it because a bare sibling-class constant is a Ruby NameError.

Top 5 recorded entries:

# Sibling class constant ambiguity

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file-wide class-scope target map accepts a residual false-positive risk when sibling classes in the same file define the same constant name. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A says this is the only real false-positive case, observed at about 1.7% of Ruby targets on Rails, and valid code rarely hits it because a bare sibling-class constant is a Ruby NameError.

# Member-name overlap ambiguity

Lifecycle status: accepted

Same-file value-reference matching accepts a bounded residual ambiguity when a shared constant name overlaps with a method, class, or sibling companion/type name in Scala/Kotlin/Swift. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#2 says Scala's interchangeable `val`/`def` members and Kotlin's val/def-or-class name overlap cannot be distinguished by same-file name matching, and Swift shares the sibling-type name-overlap bound; investigated collisions were bounded and sampled reads were genuine.

# Dart generated binding noise

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dart generated FFI/JNI binding files can inflate sibling-class ambiguity when header-only generators are not filtered, even though common generated suffixes are already excluded. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says generated Dart JNIGEN `_bindings.dart` files with many `static final _class` targets are noisy, while `.g.dart`, `.freezed.dart`, and `.pb.dart` are filtered.

# Rationale: All-language callback registrations

Lifecycle status: accepted

CHANGELOG.md#3 records callback-registration capture as a shipped all-supported-language behavior with conservative ambiguity handling, replacing the earlier whole-graph callback synthesis plan.

# Ruby constant-assignment value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Ruby value-reference support creates nodes for `CONST = ...` assignments, accepts `class:` and `module:` parents in the target gate, and scans `constant` reader nodes so class/module-internal constants can produce same-file value-reference edges. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#2 says Ruby had 0 top-level vs 58 class-internal constants in jekyll `lib/`, the original file-scope-only gate covered almost nothing, and Ruby required those three Ruby-specific fixes.

# Definition-level monorepo precision

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph must distinguish same-named symbols and types across monorepo apps, packages, files, and namespaces so callers and impact do not conflate unrelated definitions. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 same-named symbols and C# namespace-qualified type bullets.

Top 5 recorded entries:

# Background file watcher

Lifecycle status: accepted

The background file watcher is the CodeGraph server component that observes project files and triggers index updates while the MCP server runs. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 describes the watcher exhausting file descriptors on macOS and its new recursive/bounded watch strategy.

# Flat-cost recursive watcher

Lifecycle status: accepted

The background watcher now uses a single recursive watch on macOS and Windows and bounded per-directory watches on Linux. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says this replaced one open file handle per watched file, keeping watcher cost flat no matter how large the project is.

# Watch sync stale-edge tolerance

Lifecycle status: accepted

Watch sync drops a single stale edge instead of aborting the whole daemon sync with a `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` error. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

# Stale-lock watcher accuracy

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file watcher keeps edited files marked stale while another process holds the index lock, instead of marking them fresh before indexing actually succeeds. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

# Watcher excludes ignored paths

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file watcher excludes the same default and `.gitignore` directories as the indexer before registering watches, preventing large repos from exhausting OS watch budgets. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 Fixes.
